# Sublime Security - email security candidate (2026-11-05)

**Canonical entity:** Sublime Security, https://sublime.security/  
**Stage:** Researched; human review pending. Vendor-published, not independent test evidence.  
**Primary map category:** `email-security`. **Adjacent:** `dlp`, `security-awareness` (product announcements; verify edition); `itdr` only after evidence of distinct account control.

## Product and architecture
- **Vendor-reported:** programmable detection rules and Message Query Language (MQL), API connection to M365 / Google Workspace, transparent detection decisions and retrospective email hunts. [Overview](https://docs.sublime.security/docs/overview)
- **ASA:** Autonomous Security Analyst investigates user reports and suspicious/unknown messages. Default inactive; passive mode can send alerts but cannot change mail or auto-review it. Active mode applies configured, licensed per-verdict actions; unknown verdicts require human review. Switching to active does not retroactively remediate passive investigations. Available in Enterprise. [ASA docs](https://docs.sublime.security/docs/asa-autonomous-security-analyst)
- **ADÉ:** Autonomous Detection Engineer drafts organization-specific MQL rules from confirmed misses, backtests historical email and proposes approval. Human approval is the default; optional auto-activation uses a configurable backtest threshold. Activated rules can carry remediation, including quarantine for malicious rules, so activation is an enforcement decision. Enterprise includes ADÉ; self-hosted AWS may incur per-report processing costs. Backtest precision is not production efficacy. [ADÉ docs](https://docs.sublime.security/docs/ade-autonomous-detection-engineer)
- **Deployment:** Sublime Cloud or authorized self-hosted AWS / AWS GovCloud; no MX changes. Vendor documents region and processing caveats for agent inference: validate actual data flow and operating costs in selected region. [Installation](https://docs.sublime.security/docs/installation-options), [ADÉ docs](https://docs.sublime.security/docs/ade-autonomous-detection-engineer)
- **Delivery boundary:** default API processing is post-delivery. Optional Enterprise [Inline Protection](https://docs.sublime.security/docs/inline-protection-for-inbound-messages) uses provider transport/routing rules. Only quarantine prevents mailbox delivery; folder actions, uncovered mailboxes, later reclassification and fallback delivery must be evaluated separately. No MX change does not mean no mail-flow configuration.
- **As-of 2026:** Email DLP announced GA 2026-09-30, tailored phishing simulations/training GA 2026-10-06; email prompt-injection detection is documented for Enterprise/ASA. [DLP GA release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/sublime-security-launches-email-dlp-becoming-the-first-platform-to-deliver-agentic-email-security-for-both-inbound-threat-detection-and-outbound-data-protection-302893893.html), [simulation GA](https://sublime.security/blog/tailored-phishing-simulations-and-training-generally-available/), [prompt-injection docs](https://docs.sublime.security/docs/prompt-injection-detection)

## Commercial and partner position
[Current vendor plans](https://sublime.security/plans-detail/) advertise **Core free for first 100 mailboxes** and quote-only **Enterprise**. The [2026-04-28 channel announcement](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/sublime-security-launches-channel-partner-program-to-redefine-email-security-302755741.html) and [current partner page](https://sublime.security/partners/) advertise reseller/service-provider programs, deal registration, monthly usage-based billing and volume discounts. Exact units, rates, minimums, margin, white-label and contractual rights remain **Unknown**. [Training](https://sublime.security/product/phishing-simulations-training/) is an Enterprise add-on, not a standalone product. ASA/ADÉ Enterprise inclusion does not establish DLP entitlement or zero self-hosted processing costs.

**Documented provider operation:** [Multi-tenancy management](https://docs.sublime.security/docs/multi-tenancy-management) describes Enterprise enablement on request, parent/child organizations on the same instance, delegated roles and separate customer SSO. Validate permission scope and isolation in a tenant; documentation is not an isolation test. The [MDR/MSP/MSSP onboarding guide](https://docs.sublime.security/docs/onboarding-guide-mdr-msp-and-mssp-partners) plans 3–4 weeks, requires customer administrator access, per-child configuration (settings do not inherit), tuning before remediation and conversion before the 14-day trial expires. This is a documented operating model, not measured onboarding labor or profitable service delivery.

## Competitive hypotheses, not facts
- **Against AegisAI / Ocean:** programmable rules and backtests versus model-first investigations. Test outcomes and operational hours rather than assuming rules or models are categorically better.
- **Against Abnormal:** compare detection ownership, backtesting and approval workflows; Abnormal also markets custom rules and AI models, so programmability is not an exclusive distinction. Buyer may prefer an explainable tuning workflow or a less hands-on operation, depending on staffing and risk tolerance.
- **For service providers:** documented delegated tenant management is a practical starting point; self-hosting alone proves neither residency compliance nor MSSP margin. Test customer onboarding, least-privilege roles and offboarding.

## What to ask
1. Can the SOC review and roll back every ADÉ-approved rule? What happens at uncertain verdicts and in passive mode?
2. What is the real onboarding and tuning load, false-positive remediation and time to action at customer traffic scale?
3. Which editions and regions support ASA, ADÉ, DLP and phishing simulations; which inference data leaves an AWS tenant?
4. What are MSSP partner terms, per-tenant ownership, pricing minimums, renewal true-up and delegated admin?
